latestRelease.notes:
## Release Notes

Released on 2026-08-14.

### Python

- Add CPython 3.10.21, 3.11.16, and 3.12.14 ([#21138](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21138))
- Prefer newer versions and standard variants when selecting between equally prioritized Python interpreters ([#21134](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21134))

### Enhancements

- Simplify errors and hints for invalid editable requirements, and redact credentials in requirement URLs ([#21130](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21130))

### Preview features

- Allow `--index` and `--default-index` to select configured package indexes by name with the `index-by-name` preview feature ([#17455](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/17455))
- Include distribution artifact URLs and hashes in CycloneDX SBOM exports by default ([#21131](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21131))
- Fall back to logical file sizes when using `cache-physical-space` on filesystems that do not support physical-space accounting ([#21133](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21133))

### Bug fixes

- Resolve relative package index paths in PEP 723 scripts against the script directory ([#21097](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/21097))

## Install uv 0.12.5

### Install prebuilt binaries via shell script

```sh
curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.12.5/uv-installer.sh | sh
```

### Install prebuilt binaries via powershell script

```sh
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "irm https://releases.astral.sh/github/uv/releases/download/0.12.5/uv-installer.ps1 | iex"
```

## Verifying GitHub Artifact Attestations

The artifacts in this release have attestations generated with GitHub Artifact Attestations. These can be verified by using the [GitHub CLI](https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_attestation_verify):
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --repo astral-sh/uv
```

You can also download the attestation from [GitHub](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/attestations) and verify against that directly:
```sh
gh attestation verify <file-path of downloaded artifact> --bundle <file-path of downloaded attestation>
```

signals.title: How can I install project dependencies from an existing pyproject.toml?
signals.text: The official documentation doesn't clearly explain how to install project dependencies. It's all vague and indirect, with no concrete example/instructions! How am I supposed to install project dependencies from an existing pyproject.toml? Where is that notorious `uv install` command that would install all the project packages?
signals.author: alexted

signals.title: Add `uv tool upgrade --with <new_pkg>` or `--add-with <new_pkg>` to add packages to an install
signals.text: ### Summary Add `uv tool upgrade --with <new_pkg>` or `--add-with <new_pkg>` to add packages to an install. I propose the following being valid: ```bash uv tool install ipython --with requests uv tool upgrade ipython --with polars # Now, I can use both "polars" and "requests" libraries within the ipython tool. ``` ### Example For example, I have `uv tool install ipython`, then run ipython (an interactive REPL) to do some math. Then later, I do `uv tool install ipython --with polars` to run IPython and test a Polars feature quickly. Then later, I want my existing `ipython` setup, BUT I also want to install the `pint` dependency to do some math with units in that tool's environment. Currently, your only option is `uv tool install ipython --with polars --with python` to add in more. Consider that there are now 5+ dependencies I've added to my IPython tool's environment (e.g., orjson, pandas, scipy, requests). It's a lot to manage.
signals.author: DeflateAwning

signals.title: `uv tool` usage with `uv.toml` named index
signals.text: ### Question Hello, thank you for building uv. Am I able to use `uv.toml` named index with `uv tool` command? For example, let's say I have this in my user-level `uv.toml` ``` [[index]] name = "foo" url = "https://foo.org/simple" explicit = true ``` I would like to run something akin to: `uv tool install bar --index foo` And the result is that uv will attempt to install `bar` from `foo` and only `foo`. I'm not sure if I have the syntax wrong or if this is not a feature. ### Platform Windows 11 ### Version uv 0.11.7 (9d177269e 2026-04-15 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

signals.title: Add support for single-file environment
signals.text: ### Summary In my project, the Python scripts are all written in single files. Each file may have different environments. I hope that within a single Python script, I can declare the running Python version and related dependencies through comments，for example `main.py`: ```python # -*- env_name: figma_export_color -*- # -*- py_version: 3.8 -*- # -*- dependencies: [pyyaml==6.0.2, requests] -*- import sys import re import yaml import json import os ... ``` then: ```shell uv run main.py ```

signals.title: UV run package conflicts with binaries installed on the operating system
signals.text: ### Question I encountered a naming conflict between a custom Python logging library I built and the built-in macOS logger binary. My understanding is that **uvx** is designed to run globally installed binaries (either on the OS or in the UV global space), whereas **uv run** is meant for running packages in the UV global space or local Python libraries. Given this, should this naming collision be considered a bug or expected behavior? Also, uvx and uv run are intended to serve different purposes, correct? ### Platform _No response_ ### Version _No response_

signals.title: Reimplement `package.metadata`-less lockfiles
signals.text: The previous iterations of `package.metadata`-free lockfiles had missed a number of cases, and made it hard to ensure that all cases were actually covered. This PR takes a new approach: Remove the previous implementation, and then re-add it feature-by-feature in reviewable commit units. Each commit adds one feature that uv supports. The new approach is not entirely `package.metadata`-free, instead remote URL, which can activate other URL source, now have `package.metadata` which they previously didn't. That's required for offline validation (which is crucial for `uv lock --check` performance, offline or not) and IMO the more correct tradeoff: We shouldn't repeat information that's already available on disk, but we should state what we expect from remote resources. `uv.lock` revision 1.4 additionally records empty extras so `--frozen --extra foo` if the lock wasn't generated with extra `foo` present, but it was added to `pyproject.toml` afterwards. This is a lockfile size regression if you're using a lot of remote URLs, otherwise it's still a much smaller lockfile for large workspaces. Remote source are usually used sparingly as they are worse for performance, reliability and auditability than registry sources. ## Validation This change reflects basically every resolver assumption and form of dependency specification and also hits a number of preexisting bugs (see upstack PRs and skipped changes list). Instead of trying to reason through correctness from the features we're representing, this PR was tested (and fixed) against large, diverse validation set, checking that uv's invariants are upheld with lockfile revision 1.4. The PR is additionally split into one commit per feature the new freshness check support, to ease reviewing and ensure that all features are covered. The most import check that needs to always pass is `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` on a fresh lockfile. We don't need to check features such as `uv sync`, as `package.metadata` is only used for fast path freshness checks, and `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` exercises the offline fast path while blocking the slow path if it would use the internet (which is unacceptable both for performance and for checks that run in isolated environments). The goal is to cover the available dependency specification that people use, while not fixing unrelated bugs in this already large change. There are three of these larger validations. The first one is a script finds public GitHub projects with editable packages, workspaces, Git dependencies or dynamically generated dependencies and then verifies that both the original lockfile and a version with package metadata removed pass `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` inside an isolated docker container. This dataset contained 254 projects with 14k locked packages. The second validation uses the check-mode in https://github.com/astral-sh/uv-ecosystem-testing with `UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES=lock-without-metadata` . The third one is running the test suite migrated to lockfile revision 1.4 with https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/commit/4b98802626b18406a47e71fc2583bc5576934e6e, passing 4.8k tests: ``` features=test-python-patch,test-universal,native-auth cargo insta test --accept --test-runner nextest --workspace --features "$features" cargo nextest run --workspace --features "$features" ``` The PR handles the test cases and fixes from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/20803 too. ## Skipped changes The following independent bugfixes are deliberately excluded from this stack: - #21210. - #21225. The cache assertion remains a TODO here. The 4.8k-test run above included the add-cache fix and predates this extraction; it is not a fresh full-suite run of the reduced stack.

signals.title: Verify locked source archives before building metadata
signals.text: `uv.lock` records archive digests, but checking an existing lockfile or resolving with `--locked` can obtain source metadata without comparing those digests. A replaced source archive can therefore run its build backend before a later hash or lockfile check rejects it. Construct a `HashStrategy` from the existing lockfile's hashes for registry packages, direct URLs, and local archives. Enforce the recorded hashes when reusing cached source metadata, resolving with `--locked`, and installing build dependencies recorded in the lockfile into isolated build environments. Normalize equivalent archive subdirectories so they find the same recorded hashes. Keep recorded hashes while checking whether an existing lockfile is still usable, but allow unlocked fresh resolution to replace them. Build dependencies without recorded hashes remain allowed. Based on #21248, which checks source archives before saving them to the cache. #21246 contains the structural refactor, and #21247 separates hash generation from verification.

signals.title: Represent validated source archives before persistence
signals.text: Source archive helpers currently extract an archive and save it to the cache in the same call. Separate those steps so the type system records that extraction and its existing checks have completed before persistence. Introduce a private `ValidatedSourceArchive` that owns the temporary directory. Its HTTP and local constructors retain their transport setup, diagnostics, and cleanup behavior, while a private reader helper performs the shared extraction and hash collection. The consuming `persist` method saves the source tree and returns the collected hashes and byte count. This preserves existing behavior; it does not add trusted-hash comparisons or change cache repair. #21247 separates hash generation from verification, and #21248 checks caller-supplied hashes before persistence.
signals.author: zanieb

signals.title: Separate hash generation policy from verification policy
signals.text: `HashStrategy` currently represents hash generation and verification as mutually exclusive choices. A resolution may need both: verify artifacts whose hashes have been supplied, while generating hashes for new artifacts. Store generation separately from `HashVerification` in `HashStrategy`. Each distribution still receives a `HashPolicy` specifying whether to generate or check hashes. Update existing call sites to use the separate settings while preserving their hash inputs and which hashes uv treats as trusted. Generation remains available for artifacts without supplied hashes, unless the caller requires a hash for every artifact. This does not read hashes from `uv.lock` or add new archive comparisons. Based on #21246. #21248 checks caller-supplied hashes before source archives enter the cache. #21223 reads hashes from an existing `uv.lock` and supplies them for verification.
signals.author: zanieb

signals.title: Validate source archives before cache persistence
signals.text: Source archives can be saved to the cache before their caller-supplied hashes are checked. Cache repair can also save replacement contents before detecting a mismatch with the previous revision. Check supplied hashes alongside the existing download-size check in `ValidatedSourceArchive::extract`, before it returns the value consumed by `persist`. Check every digest from a previous revision there too, before a repaired source tree is saved. Extraction still streams into a private temporary directory and returns parser errors immediately. This also removes the split in persistence behavior captured by `ArchiveOrigin`. HTTP and local archives now accept `AlreadyExists` or `DirectoryNotEmpty` only when the destination is a directory, and both retain temporary-directory ownership through persistence. The HTTP path no longer calls `TempDir::keep` for archives with multiple top-level entries, so failed persistence attempts clean up those staged files too. HTTP response handling and local file opening remain separate, and cache locations and `rename_with_retry` are unchanged. The caller still supplies the hashes and any download size to check; this PR does not read trusted hashes from `uv.lock`. #21223 supplies the hashes recorded in an existing `uv.lock`. Based on #21247.

signals.title: Portable Environments
signals.text: ## Summary Add `--preview portable-envs` which makes relocatable environments backed by uv-managed Pythons "portable" or "real" environments which contain their own Python interpreter and can be moved between compatible machines. ## Notes Global `--preview` will enable this feature for all eligible environments. I think this might be a bit too much, but wasn't sure how to gate it. I am open for suggestions. This patches `libpython.dylib` to be relative to `@executable_path`. This means executables linking against `libpython` will work once they're in the virtual environment's `bin` directory, and will work when moved around. But executables not in the `bin` directory will _not_ work because `@executable_path` won't be in the right place. There's not much that can be done to fix this, AIUI... See also: #10598 This patches `_sysconfigdata_*.py` to make it portable. But it does it only for portable environments. I think it might be safe-ish to just do it always? Not sure. ## Test Plan A bunch of new tests covering corner cases nobody could have even imagined.

signal.title: Represent validated source archives before persistence
signal.text: Source archive helpers currently extract an archive and save it to the cache in the same call. Separate those steps so the type system records that extraction and its existing checks have completed before persistence. Introduce a private `ValidatedSourceArchive` that owns the temporary directory. Its HTTP and local constructors retain their transport setup, diagnostics, and cleanup behavior, while a private reader helper performs the shared extraction and hash collection. The consuming `persist` method saves the source tree and returns the collected hashes and byte count. This preserves existing behavior; it does not add trusted-hash comparisons or change cache repair. #21247 separates hash generation from verification, and #21248 checks caller-supplied hashes before persistence.

signal.title: Validate source archives before cache persistence
signal.text: Source archives can be saved to the cache before their caller-supplied hashes are checked. Cache repair can also save replacement contents before detecting a mismatch with the previous revision. Check supplied hashes alongside the existing download-size check in `ValidatedSourceArchive::extract`, before it returns the value consumed by `persist`. Check every digest from a previous revision there too, before a repaired source tree is saved. Extraction still streams into a private temporary directory and returns parser errors immediately. This also removes the split in persistence behavior captured by `ArchiveOrigin`. HTTP and local archives now accept `AlreadyExists` or `DirectoryNotEmpty` only when the destination is a directory, and both retain temporary-directory ownership through persistence. The HTTP path no longer calls `TempDir::keep` for archives with multiple top-level entries, so failed persistence attempts clean up those staged files too. HTTP response handling and local file opening remain separate, and cache locations and `rename_with_retry` are unchanged. The caller still supplies the hashes and any download size to check; this PR does not read trusted hashes from `uv.lock`. #21223 supplies the hashes recorded in an existing `uv.lock`. Based on #21247.
signal.author: zanieb

signal.title: Separate hash generation policy from verification policy
signal.text: `HashStrategy` currently represents hash generation and verification as mutually exclusive choices. A resolution may need both: verify artifacts whose hashes have been supplied, while generating hashes for new artifacts. Store generation separately from `HashVerification` in `HashStrategy`. Each distribution still receives a `HashPolicy` specifying whether to generate or check hashes. Update existing call sites to use the separate settings while preserving their hash inputs and which hashes uv treats as trusted. Generation remains available for artifacts without supplied hashes, unless the caller requires a hash for every artifact. This does not read hashes from `uv.lock` or add new archive comparisons. Based on #21246. #21248 checks caller-supplied hashes before source archives enter the cache. #21223 reads hashes from an existing `uv.lock` and supplies them for verification.
signal.author: zanieb

signal.title: Verify locked source archives before building metadata
signal.text: `uv.lock` records archive digests, but checking an existing lockfile or resolving with `--locked` can obtain source metadata without comparing those digests. A replaced source archive can therefore run its build backend before a later hash or lockfile check rejects it. Construct a `HashStrategy` from the existing lockfile's hashes for registry packages, direct URLs, and local archives. Enforce the recorded hashes when reusing cached source metadata, resolving with `--locked`, and installing build dependencies recorded in the lockfile into isolated build environments. Normalize equivalent archive subdirectories so they find the same recorded hashes. Keep recorded hashes while checking whether an existing lockfile is still usable, but allow unlocked fresh resolution to replace them. Build dependencies without recorded hashes remain allowed. Based on #21248, which checks source archives before saving them to the cache. #21246 contains the structural refactor, and #21247 separates hash generation from verification.

signal.title: Reimplement `package.metadata`-less lockfiles
signal.text: The previous iterations of `package.metadata`-free lockfiles had missed a number of cases, and made it hard to ensure that all cases were actually covered. This PR takes a new approach: Remove the previous implementation, and then re-add it feature-by-feature in reviewable commit units. Each commit adds one feature that uv supports. The new approach is not entirely `package.metadata`-free, instead remote URL, which can activate other URL source, now have `package.metadata` which they previously didn't. That's required for offline validation (which is crucial for `uv lock --check` performance, offline or not) and IMO the more correct tradeoff: We shouldn't repeat information that's already available on disk, but we should state what we expect from remote resources. `uv.lock` revision 1.4 additionally records empty extras so `--frozen --extra foo` if the lock wasn't generated with extra `foo` present, but it was added to `pyproject.toml` afterwards. This is a lockfile size regression if you're using a lot of remote URLs, otherwise it's still a much smaller lockfile for large workspaces. Remote source are usually used sparingly as they are worse for performance, reliability and auditability than registry sources. ## Validation This change reflects basically every resolver assumption and form of dependency specification and also hits a number of preexisting bugs (see upstack PRs and skipped changes list). Instead of trying to reason through correctness from the features we're representing, this PR was tested (and fixed) against large, diverse validation set, checking that uv's invariants are upheld with lockfile revision 1.4. The PR is additionally split into one commit per feature the new freshness check support, to ease reviewing and ensure that all features are covered. The most import check that needs to always pass is `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` on a fresh lockfile. We don't need to check features such as `uv sync`, as `package.metadata` is only used for fast path freshness checks, and `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` exercises the offline fast path while blocking the slow path if it would use the internet (which is unacceptable both for performance and for checks that run in isolated environments). The goal is to cover the available dependency specification that people use, while not fixing unrelated bugs in this already large change. There are three of these larger validations. The first one is a script finds public GitHub projects with editable packages, workspaces, Git dependencies or dynamically generated dependencies and then verifies that both the original lockfile and a version with package metadata removed pass `uv lock --check --offline --no-cache` inside an isolated docker container. This dataset contained 254 projects with 14k locked packages. The second validation uses the check-mode in https://github.com/astral-sh/uv-ecosystem-testing with `UV_PREVIEW_FEATURES=lock-without-metadata` . The third one is running the test suite migrated to lockfile revision 1.4 with https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/commit/4b98802626b18406a47e71fc2583bc5576934e6e, passing 4.8k tests: ``` features=test-python-patch,test-universal,native-auth cargo insta test --accept --test-runner nextest --workspace --features "$features" cargo nextest run --workspace --features "$features" ``` The PR handles the test cases and fixes from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/20803 too. ## Skipped changes The following independent bugfixes are deliberately excluded from this stack: - #21210. - #21225. The cache assertion remains a TODO here. The 4.8k-test run above included the add-cache fix and predates this extraction; it is not a fresh full-suite run of the reduced stack.

signal.title: Portable Environments
signal.text: ## Summary Add `--preview portable-envs` which makes relocatable environments backed by uv-managed Pythons "portable" or "real" environments which contain their own Python interpreter and can be moved between compatible machines. ## Notes Global `--preview` will enable this feature for all eligible environments. I think this might be a bit too much, but wasn't sure how to gate it. I am open for suggestions. This patches `libpython.dylib` to be relative to `@executable_path`. This means executables linking against `libpython` will work once they're in the virtual environment's `bin` directory, and will work when moved around. But executables not in the `bin` directory will _not_ work because `@executable_path` won't be in the right place. There's not much that can be done to fix this, AIUI... See also: #10598 This patches `_sysconfigdata_*.py` to make it portable. But it does it only for portable environments. I think it might be safe-ish to just do it always? Not sure. ## Test Plan A bunch of new tests covering corner cases nobody could have even imagined.

signal.title: Add `uv tool upgrade --with <new_pkg>` or `--add-with <new_pkg>` to add packages to an install
signal.text: ### Summary Add `uv tool upgrade --with <new_pkg>` or `--add-with <new_pkg>` to add packages to an install. I propose the following being valid: ```bash uv tool install ipython --with requests uv tool upgrade ipython --with polars # Now, I can use both "polars" and "requests" libraries within the ipython tool. ``` ### Example For example, I have `uv tool install ipython`, then run ipython (an interactive REPL) to do some math. Then later, I do `uv tool install ipython --with polars` to run IPython and test a Polars feature quickly. Then later, I want my existing `ipython` setup, BUT I also want to install the `pint` dependency to do some math with units in that tool's environment. Currently, your only option is `uv tool install ipython --with polars --with python` to add in more. Consider that there are now 5+ dependencies I've added to my IPython tool's environment (e.g., orjson, pandas, scipy, requests). It's a lot to manage.
